message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.00794 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Second ionization energy | 27.211 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~53 pm |
| | Covalent radius | ~31 pm |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (¹H), 0 (²H), ½ (³H) |
| | Relative abundance | ¹H ≈ 99.98 %, ²H ≈ 0.02 % |
| | Radioactivity | ³H is β‑emitter (half‑life ≈ 12.32 y) |
| **Physical** | State at RT | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density at STP | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (STP) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Specific heat ratio (γ) | 1.41 |
| | Speed of sound (in H₂) | ~1275 m s⁻¹ |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 × 10⁻³ M (at 25 °C) |
| | Vapor pressure (at 25 °C) | 1.3 × 10⁵ Pa (≈1 atm) |
| **Chemical** | Bond type | Covalent (H–H single bond) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as hydride H⁻) |
| | Acidic behavior | Forms H⁺ (proton) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride H⁻ with metals (forming metal hydrides) |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with O₂ → H₂O, with halogens → HX, with metals → metal hydrides |
| | Explosive limits (air) | Lower limit 4 % vol, upper limit 75 % vol |
| | Combustion enthalpy | –285.83 kJ mol⁻¹ (formation of H₂O from H₂ & O₂) |
| | Uses | Fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX), ammonia synthesis, hydrogenation reactions, metallurgy, semiconductor manufacturing, etc. |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (produces only water vapor); however, large-scale production often relies on fossil fuels (steam reforming) which emits CO₂ unless coupled with carbon capture. |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element** – lowest density among gases; ideal for buoyancy applications (balloons, aircraft).
- **Most abundant element in the Universe** – ~75 % of baryonic mass in stars and interstellar medium.
- **Isotopic significance** – Deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; Tritium used in nuclear weapons and fusion reactors.
- **Chemical versatility** – Forms acids (HX), bases (hydroxides), salts (hydrides), and organometallic compounds.
- **Energy carrier** – Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity with only water as exhaust; potential for zero‑emission transportation.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
